text: This game is difficult, sometimes frustrating, and absolutely unforgiving, but that's also what makes finally overcoming something feel so satisfying. Every death teaches you something, and every successful attempt feels earned. The atmosphere and combat make it even better, and despite all the times this game has destroyed me, I still keep coming back for another attempt.

Pretty solid. Should be of interest to enjoyers of understated world building and minimalist gameplay. Obviously, game takes a lot of inspiration from Limbo both aesthetically and even with some mechanics.

One of my gripes is that your diver guy has inertia and turns pretty slowly and some fish you get to control are quite clumsy also, which is what what you'd expect from the underwater game and is not a problem most of the time. But towards the last chapter game relies too much on having you avoid deadly hazards precisely

Fortunately the game is concise. So the frustrations that you may have don't accumulate that badly. All in all, worth a try, I'd say

A ~10 hourish point and click adventure. Also a bleak and particular American gothic story set at the very outermost fringes of what appears to be a capitalist nightmare dystopian "cyberpunk" hellscape. Our story takes place in a dying town being consumed by self-fulfilling industrial expansion, an estranged family trauma with a mother consumed by cancer, viral extremist religious cults that ultimately eat their own, and outright cosmic horror...all looking like different aspects of the same thing. It's pretty good.

A love letter to epic, sprawling, narrative-driven JRPGs of the past with a very unique premise. Gameplay of course takes a more reactive, and action-inspired approach of souslike games, especially parry-forward ones; and mostly succeeds, however there are some potential balancing issues especially towards the end of the game (or maybe non-issue if you enjoy power fantasies and creating overpowered builds that can trivialize encounters). Narrative, music, art design, is top notch. Everything in this game was made with care and detail and it shows in spades.

Bright Memory is a short FPS with surprisingly satisfying combat. The shooting feels great, and the fast-paced gameplay is a lot of fun. The dodge mechanic is a cool addition, although accidentally triggering it by double-tapping a movement key can get annoying.

The story is probably my biggest issue. There isn’t much context or explanation, so it can be pretty confusing. Hopefully, Bright Memory: Infinite expands on the story and gives more context.

The graphics are also quite impressive, especially for such a short game.

Overall, I enjoyed my time with it.
